time.tai_source: kernel adjtimex (ret=0, status=0x2000) — read, not hardcoded

discipline.reference: u-blox ZED-F9T TP1 PPS, FALLING edge on the second
discipline.path: ZED-F9T (hosted on f9t) -> coax -> i210 SDP0 -> ts2phc -> /dev/ptp0

precision.honest_summary: The i210 PHC tracks the GNSS PPS to ~9.81 ns RMS, but this timestamp was READ from userspace at a cost of ~27000 ns. Treat the stamp as good to ~27000 ns (tens of microseconds), NOT to nanoseconds. The nanosecond figures describe the clock, not the stamp.
uncalibrated_terms: GNSS antenna cable delay (69 ns is configured in the F9T; we have not verified it)
PPS coax length from the F9T TP1 to the i210 SDP0 input
i210 SDP0 input latency / edge-detect offset
the ZED-F9T receiver's own accuracy with respect to UTC(k)

disclosure.signed_payload: sha256 of canonical(core); both signatures cover the same digest
disclosure.what_this_proves: The pulse has not been altered since signing, and two independent hosts attested it. The time field is when f9t read its clock, not when it signed; the gap is the latency above.
disclosure.what_this_does_NOT_prove: It does not prove the value was unknown before publication. v0 has a single publisher and no external anchor. Do not use a pulse for any draw whose result matters unless it is combined with a participant-supplied nonce.
disclosure.time_precision_vs_accuracy: We claim PRECISION (how tightly the PHC tracks the GNSS PPS) and traceability of the discipline chain. We do NOT claim calibrated absolute accuracy versus UTC(k); the cable and input-latency terms are uncalibrated and listed in core.time.precision.uncalibrated_terms.
disclosure.not_certified: Not NIST/FIPS/CC validated. Not an accredited service. See CLAIMS.md.
